disposition_reason: Prints mean and SD of zinc, copper, lead and cadmium in raw milk from 22 Tehran districts and in packaged low, semi and full fat and flavored milks of 15 brands.

study.design: market and bulk-tank survey: raw milk from 22 districts and packaged (pasteurized and sterilized) milks by brand, fat level and flavor
study.origin: raw milk: bulk milk tanks in 22 districts of Tehran; packaged milk origin not stated

period.as_reported: raw and packaged milk collected during early-morning milking in summer 2016

study.method: differential pulse anodic stripping voltammetry (HMDE) with standard addition, triplicate measurements
lod: DPASV limits: Zn 0.05, Cu 0.01, Pb 0.005, Cd 0.005 mg/kg
study.qa: precision 5.6%, 3.2%, 3.5%, 4.5% (Zn, Cu, Pb, Cd); no CRM or recovery reported

findings.group: all samples, Tehran (raw milk from 22 districts; packaged milk of 15 brands)
findings.notes: Table 1 prints no unit; the abstract gives these means in µg/mL, so the per-litre unit is kept and value_ugkg is null (Tables 2-7 use mg/kg). Abstract prints raw Zn 4.990.

controls.control: commercial heat processing and packaging (pasteurized/sterilized milk)
controls.outcome: Pb 0.271 -> 0.048, Cd 0.099 -> 0.049, Zn 4.989 -> 0.999, Cu 2.424 -> 0.228 (µg/mL per abstract); t-test significant for Pb (p=0.009), Zn and Cu, not Cd (p=0.113); different milks, not paired

unresolved: Printed DOI 10.22034/jchr.2020.1877927.1048 (manifest had none); used as printed.
Sample numbers unclear: text says 30 raw and 26 packaged samples, but Table 3 alone has 45 brand-by-fat rows plus 36 flavored rows; per-row n not given.
Table 1 has no unit; abstract gives µg/mL. Tables 2-7 are mg/kg. The paper says all lead values were below 20 µg/kg, which contradicts its own lead means (e.g., raw milk 0.271).
Many SDs exceed their means and some means fall below the stated detection limits (flagged).
Peer review unverified: received/accepted dates printed, no review record seen. Acknowledgment says it was a student thesis.
